title: Managed LLM Platforms — Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI

questions.question: Which entry in PLATFORMS has no PTU offering in the local comparator?
options: All three expose the same PTU field
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Gemini stores ptu_hourly as None and ptu_tokens_per_hour as 0; Bedrock and Azure have PTU values.

questions.question: Azure's PTU advertises 2,000,000 tokens/hour. How much daily capacity does one PTU provide in the demo?
questions.explanation: The comparator multiplies ptu_tokens_per_hour by 24, so Azure's unit supplies 2,000,000 × 24 = 48,000,000 tokens/day.

questions.question: With 3M input and 1M output tokens, what on-demand daily cost does Bedrock compute?
questions.explanation: Bedrock charges $3/M input and $15/M output, giving 3×3 + 1×15 = $24 for the workload.

questions.question: Why can the PTU-enabled Azure run still print the on-demand path for a 45M-token workload?
options: Azure PTUs are never considered when use_ptu is true
The PTU path always has higher TTFT, so it is rejected
The code compares only median TTFT and ignores cost
questions.explanation: simulate computes both costs and uses min(cost_ondemand, cost_ptu); a PTU is not selected merely because use_ptu is enabled.

questions.question: Which Azure latency value represents the dedicated PTU median in the platform table?
questions.explanation: Azure's Platform row sets ttft_median_ms to 50 for shared capacity and ttft_median_ptu_ms to 38 for a PTU.

questions.question: The lock-in example adds 3% gateway overhead and 10% idle secondary headroom. What uplift does it report?
questions.explanation: lock_in_cost adds the two percentages, so the redundancy uplift is 3% + 10% = 13% of primary daily spend.
